title: Space technology's economic impact must go beyond launches, manufacturing: Jitendra Singh

ai.summary: Union Minister Jitendra Singh stated that India's space technology economic impact should include sectoral savings and efficiencies beyond launches and manufacturing, with the space economy projected to grow from USD 9 billion to USD 40-45 billion in a decade.

facts.claim: space technology's economic impact must be measured not only through rocket launches, satellite manufacturing, and commercial revenues but also through savings, efficiencies, and improved outcomes
facts.quote: The economic contribution of space technology must be measured not only through rocket launches, satellite manufacturing, and commercial revenues but also through the savings, efficiencies, and improved outcomes it generates across sectors on the ground

facts.claim: space-based applications help improve infrastructure planning, maintain project timelines, reduce costs, and minimise wastage and leakages
facts.quote: space-based applications help improve infrastructure planning, maintain project timelines, reduce costs, and minimise wastage and leakages

facts.claim: India's space economy is valued at nearly USD 9 billion and projected to grow to USD 40-45 billion in less than a decade
facts.quote: India's space economy, currently valued at nearly USD 9 billion, is set to grow to USD 40-45 billion in less than a decade

facts.claim: India's space ecosystem has expanded from single-digit startups to nearly 400-500 companies in a few years
facts.quote: India's space ecosystem has expanded from single-digit startups to nearly 400-500 companies in just a few years
